item.title: Nestle Sells Vitamins Business to Private Equity for $1 Billion
item.description: Nestle SA plans to sell its mainstream vitamins and supplements business to US private equity firm Yellow Wood Partners for $1 billion as Chief Executive Officer Philipp Navratil tries to streamline and turn around the Swiss foodmaker.

item.title: Apple Ternus Touts Product Pipeline, ‘Phenomenal’ Sept. 9 iPhone Launch in Memo
item.description: Apple Inc. Chief Executive Officer John Ternus touted the company’s strong product pipeline and teased a “phenomenal” iPhone launch next week in his first remarks to employees as their new leader.

item.title: Bessent Suggests Backing for BOJ Action in Meeting With Ueda
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who’s repeatedly signaled that Japan needs higher interest rates to bolster the yen, suggested he’s supporting such a move after a meeting with Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda.

item.title: Apple’s Former CFO Maestri Drops Role Running Corporate Services
item.description: With John Ternus beginning his role as Apple Inc. chief executive officer this week, another mainstay from the Tim Cook era is dropping his late-career responsibilities.

item.title: Bond Market Selloff: Are Surging Yields a Threat to the Global Stock Rally?
item.description: In equity markets, the myth goes that the only way is up. That perception has gained traction as global stock prices have largely ignored the selloff in bond markets. Yields on long-dated government debt have surged to near two-decade highs as investors worry about whether inflation and fiscal deficits can be tamed, and as sovereign bonds compete with an AI-fueled corporate borrowing boom.

item.title: Robinhood’s Prediction Market Growth Makes Morgan Stanley a Bull
item.description: Robinhood Markets Inc.’s prediction markets efforts offer a “proof point” that the online brokerage can keep expanding revenue, according to Morgan Stanley analyst Michael Cyprys.

item.title: Uruguay acelera desdolarización con nuevos fondos Money Market
item.description: Los inversores en Uruguay están colocando una mayor parte de su patrimonio en fondos Money Market y bonos del gobierno en pesos, lo que da un mayor impulso a los esfuerzos de este país sudamericano, considerado un refugio seguro, por reducir su dependencia del dólar.

item.title: Carney Says Trade Talks Can Resume If US Stops ‘Throwing Shade’
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney said he still believes there’s a “mutually beneficial” trade deal to be done with the US, but discussions can’t resume while Trump administration officials are publicly insulting Canada.

item.title: Wells Fargo Analysts Join JPMorgan Traders in Turning Cautious on US Stocks
item.description: Wells Fargo & Co. is the second bank to turn cautious on US stocks this week as the market heads into what is historically the worst month on the calendar for equities and upcoming midterm elections add to uncertainty surrounding the artificial-intelligence trade.

item.title: EU Considers Front-Loading Ukraine Loan as Funding Shortage Hits
item.description: European Union member states are considering accelerating payments from the bloc’s €90 billion ($104 billion) loan to Ukraine as Kyiv faces a funding crunch, the bloc’s rotating presidency said.

item.title: Senegal Says Will Rework Debt as it Reaches New IMF Deal
item.description: Senegal’s eurobonds fell on Tuesday after the government said it will move forward with a “debt treatment” under the Group of 20’s Common Framework and agreed a new $2.2 billion financing program with the International Monetary Fund.

item.title: Airbnb Replaces Business Chief With Ex-Tripadvisor, Booking Exec
item.description: Airbnb Inc. has replaced its chief business officer with a former executive of Tripadvisor Inc. and Booking Holdings Inc., underscoring its efforts to expand beyond home-sharing into new travel segments.

item.title: Sonos Debuts $449 Ace Ultra Headphones, $699 Beam Ultra Soundbar, ChatGPT Tie-In
item.description: As the company opens its platform to AI assistants, Chief Executive Officer Tom Conrad wants to reposition Sonos as something bigger than a speaker brand.

item.title: Peru Inflation Just Tops Estimate to Hit Fastest Since 2023
item.description: Inflation in Peru’s capital accelerated slightly more than expected in August, hitting the fastest pace in almost three years, pressured by housing and utilities including electricity and gas.

item.title: Apollo’s Brightspeed Casts Going Concern Doubt as Revenue Slides
item.description: Brightspeed, the broadband provider backed by Apollo Global Management Inc., warned investors that there’s substantial doubt it will be able to continue as a going concern, as it presses ahead with its search for financing to meet looming debt obligations.

item.title: US Job Openings Edge Higher in Sign of Stable Labor Demand
item.description: US job openings edged higher in July and layoffs fell, suggesting demand for workers remains stable at a subdued level.

item.title: Dell, HP Enterprise Need Earnings to Validate Record Stock Runs
item.description: Artificial intelligence fever is powering Dell Technologies Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. to their best years in the stock market.

item.title: Waymo Expands Paid Robotaxi Rides to Denver, San Diego and Tampa
item.description: Waymo will begin offering paid robotaxi rides to the public in Denver, San Diego, and Tampa, Florida, bringing the number of US cities where its driverless ride-hail service is available to 14.

item.title: US Factory Gauge Eases But Holds Close to Four-Year High
item.description: US manufacturing activity expanded for an eighth straight month in August, though a moderation in new order and employment growth signaled some cooling in factory demand.

item.title: ECB’s September Hike Won’t Be Enough, Simkus Tells Econostream
item.description: An increase in interest rates next week by the European Central Bank won’t be sufficient to get inflation back to target, according to Governing Council member Gediminas Simkus.

item.title: ECB’s Nagel Says Slowdown in Underlying Inflation Is Good News
item.description: Slower underlying inflation in the euro zone in August is a positive development, according to European Central Bank Governing Council member Joachim Nagel.

item.title: Fervo Shares Surge on Geothermal Power Deal With Google
item.description: Shares of Fervo Energy Co. surged Tuesday after the geothermal developer signed a deal to sell almost 400 megawatts of power to Alphabet Inc.’s Google for a prospective data center in Utah.

item.title: US Stock Futures Drop as Rising Oil Prices Stoke Inflation Fears
item.description: US stock futures skidded on Tuesday, with traders bracing for interest-rate ‌hikes as renewed Middle East tensions lifted oil prices and bond yields, stoking inflation fears.

item.title: Israel Slashes Interest Rates for Third Consecutive Meeting
item.description: Israel lowered interest rates on Monday, in a decision that comes as exporters push the central bank to do more to counter the shekel’s appreciation.

item.title: China Unlikely to Match ASML’s Top Tool in Next Decade, UBS Says
item.description: China is unlikely to advance its semiconductor manufacturing capabilities fast enough to develop a viable alternative to ASML Holding NV’s cutting-edge extreme ultraviolet technology within the next decade, UBS Group AG analysts predict.

item.title: Fed’s Barr Says Higher Rates Needed If Inflation Doesn’t Cool
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said the central bank should be prepared to raise interest rates if inflation fails to subside, warning price pressures are at risk of becoming entrenched after being above target for more than five years.

item.title: Roku Launches Its First OLED TVs, With Prices Starting at $999
item.description: Roku Inc. introduced its first self-branded smart TVs with organic light emitting diode, or OLED, display technology, which will lend the new models greater contrast and punchier black levels than previous first-party Roku TVs.

item.title: Chile Economic Activity Posts Biggest Monthly Drop Since 2022
item.description: Chile’s economy contracted much more than expected in July as deadly rainstorms temporarily halted some mining operations, according to the central bank’s main monthly gauge of activity.

item.title: Saudi Video Game Giant Savvy CEO Brian Ward Is Stepping Down
item.description: Savvy Games Group Chief Executive Officer Brian Ward, who oversaw the Saudi Arabian government’s $38 billion investment in the video-game industry, is stepping down, according to a message he sent to staff on Tuesday that was reviewed by Bloomberg News.

item.title: Brazil Economy Loses Steam as High Rates Bite Before Vote
item.description: Brazil’s economy saw a modest expansion in the second quarter after a stronger start to the year as high interest rates dragged on growth ahead of the presidential election.
